briefdescription.para: Defines the status callback type for the QSPIPSU device.

detaileddescription.para: The handler data type defines a callback function that handles the asynchronous processing for the QSPIPSU device. The application using this driver defines a handler of this type to support interrupt-driven mode. The handler executes in an interrupt context, so it must perform only minimal processing.

parameterdescription.para: Callback reference passed in by the upper layer when setting the callback functions, and passed back to the upper layer when the callback is invoked. Its type is not important to the driver, so it is a void pointer.
Holds one or more status events that have occurred. See XQspiPsu_SetStatusHandler() for details on the status events that can be passed in the callback.
Indicates how many bytes of data were successfully transferred. This may be less than the number of bytes requested if the status event indicates an error.

In XSCT/classic flow, the driver uses DeviceId to look up the device configuration.

briefdescription.para: Initializes an XQspiPsu instance so that the driver is ready to use.

parameterdescription.para: Reference to a structure containing information about a specific QSPIPSU device. This function initializes an InstancePtr object for a specific device specified by the contents of Config.

Device base address in the virtual memory address space. The caller is responsible for keeping the address mapping from EffectiveAddr to the device physical base address unchanged once this function is invoked. Unexpected errors may occur if the address mapping changes after this function is called. If address translation is not used, use ConfigPtr->BaseAddress for this device.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS if successful.
XST_DEVICE_IS_STARTED if the device is already started. It must be stopped to re-initialize.

detaileddescription.para: Reset must only be called after the driver has been initialized. Any data transfer that is in progress is aborted.
The upper layer software is responsible for re-configuring (if necessary) and restarting the QSPIPSU device after the reset.

briefdescription.para: Performs a transfer on the bus in polled mode.

detaileddescription.para: The messages passed are all transferred on the bus between one CS assert and de-assert.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS if successful.
XST_FAILURE if transfer fails.

briefdescription.para: Initiates a transfer on the bus and enables interrupts.

detaileddescription.para: The interrupt handler completes the transfer. The messages passed are all transferred on the bus between one CS assert and de-assert.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the structure containing transfer data.
Number of messages to be transferred.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS if successful.
XST_FAILURE if transfer fails.
XST_DEVICE_BUSY if a transfer is already in progress.

detaileddescription.para: Acts on the GENFIFO and DMA interrupts.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS if successful.
XST_FAILURE if transfer fails.

detaileddescription.para: The driver calls the status handler when it encounters conditions that should be reported to upper layer software. The handler executes in an interrupt context, so it must minimize the amount of processing performed. One of the following status events is passed to the status handler.

para.preformatted: XST_SPI_TRANSFER_DONE The requested data transfer is done

XST_SPI_TRANSMIT_UNDERRUN As a slave device, the master clocked data but there were none available in the transmit register/FIFO. This typically means the slave application did not issue a transfer request fast enough, or the processor/driver could not fill the transmit register/FIFO fast enough.
XST_SPI_RECEIVE_OVERRUN The QSPIPSU device lost data. Data was received but the receive data register/FIFO was full.

parameterdescription.para: Upper layer callback reference passed back when the callback function is invoked.

simplesect.para: The handler is called within interrupt context, so it must do its work quickly and queue potentially time-consuming work to a task-level thread.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the structure containing transfer data.
Number of messages to be transferred.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS if successful.
XST_FAILURE if ByteCount is greater than XQSPIPSU_DMA_BYTES_MAX.
XST_DEVICE_BUSY if a transfer is already in progress.
XST_SUCCESS if DMA transfer complete.
XST_FAILURE if DMA transfer is not completed.

briefdescription.para: Configures the clock according to the prescaler passed.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS if successful.
XST_DEVICE_IS_STARTED if the device is already started.
XST_DEVICE_BUSY if the device is currently transferring data. It must be stopped to re-initialize.
XST_FAILURE if Prescaler value is less than FreqDiv when feedback clock is not enabled.

briefdescription.para: Sets the hardware flash configuration used by the QSPIPSU driver.

detaileddescription.para: Call this API at least once in the application. It can also be called multiple times when switching between different flash devices or configurations.

simplesect.para: If the application never calls this function, the driver assumes a single flash connected to the lower bus and CS line.

briefdescription.para: Sets the options for the QSPIPSU device driver.

detaileddescription.para: The options control how the device behaves relative to the QSPIPSU bus. The device must be idle rather than busy transferring data before setting these device options.

parameterdescription.para: Contains the specified options to be set. This is a bit mask where a 1 indicates the option should be turned ON and a 0 indicates no action. One or more bit values may be contained in the mask. See the bit definitions named XQSPIPSU_*_OPTIONS in the file xqspipsu.h.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS if options are successfully set.
XST_DEVICE_BUSY if the device is currently transferring data. The transfer must complete or be aborted before setting options.

briefdescription.para: Resets the options for the QSPIPSU device driver.

detaileddescription.para: The options control how the device behaves relative to the QSPIPSU bus. The device must be idle rather than busy transferring data before setting these device options.

parameterdescription.para: Contains the specified options to be set. This is a bit mask where a 1 indicates the option should be turned OFF and a 0 indicates no action. One or more bit values may be contained in the mask. See the bit definitions named XQSPIPSU_*_OPTIONS in the file xqspipsu.h.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS if options are successfully set.
XST_DEVICE_BUSY if the device is currently transferring data. The transfer must complete or be aborted before setting options.

briefdescription.para: Gets the options for the QSPIPSU device.

detaileddescription.para: The options control how the device behaves relative to the QSPIPSU bus.

simplesect.para: Options contains the specified options currently set. This is a bit value where a 1 means the option is on, and a 0 means the option is off. See the bit definitions named XQSPIPSU_*_OPTIONS in file xqspipsu.h.

briefdescription.para: Sets the Read mode for the QSPIPSU device driver.

detaileddescription.para: The device must be idle rather than busy transferring data before setting Read mode options.

parameterdescription.para: Contains the specified Mode to be set. See the bit definitions named XQSPIPSU_READMODE_* in the file xqspipsu.h.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS if options are successfully set.
XST_DEVICE_BUSY if the device is currently transferring data. The transfer must complete or be aborted before setting Mode.

briefdescription.para: Sets the Write Protect and Hold options for the QSPIPSU device driver.

detaileddescription.para: The device must be idle rather than busy transferring data before setting Write Protect and Hold options.

parameterdescription.para: Value of the WP_HOLD bit in configuration register.

simplesect.para: This function is not thread-safe. This function can only be used with single flash configuration and x1/x2 data mode. This function cannot be used with x4 data mode and dual parallel and stacked flash configuration.

briefdescription.para: Enables or disables the Write Protect pin on the flash parts.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the QSPIPSU driver component to use.

simplesect.para: By default, the QSPI controller drives the Write Protect pin High, which means no write protection. Calling this function once enables the protection.

briefdescription.para: Pauses the DMA stream and memory write operations.

detaileddescription.para: Stops the transfer of data to internal DST FIFO from stream interface and also stops the issuing of new write commands to memory.
Calling this API pauses any ongoing DMA transfers, and the DMA does not issue AXI write commands to memory.
